key_insight: Tree-based machine learning models can accurately predict band gaps across diverse halide perovskite families using simple atomic and structural descriptors.
engineering_relevance: These models help screen lead-free perovskite compositions faster, guiding the design of optoelectronic materials with target band gaps.
method: Trained ensemble tree-based regressors on atomic and structural descriptors from multiple halide perovskite types.
Compared random forest regression, gradient boosted regression trees, and extreme gradient boosting for band gap prediction.
Used feature-importance analysis to identify the most influential B-site, X-site, and site-count descriptors.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports strong predictive accuracy from several tree-based models across a wide range of halide perovskite band gaps.
watch_item: Feature importance is model-dependent, so the identified descriptors should be validated against independent datasets or physics-based analysis before design decisions.
paper_title: Machine learning insights into band gap properties in halide-based perovskites
